extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, research-integrity stakeholders, and general readers interested in retractions and misconduct
extracted.subtask_description: A news-style report describing allegations of image manipulation and data fabrication, institutional investigations, journal responses (retractions/holds/rejections), and related procedural issues in academic publishing. Useful for understanding how journals and institutions handle suspected research misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image manipulation / figure duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation that authors 'copied, flipped, and the pasted one control panel into a separate experiment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure duplication or alteration (copying/flipping/pasting panels across experiments) is a form of problematic image manipulation that can trigger investigations and lead to retraction if wrongdoing is confirmed; editors and institutions should scrutinize questioned figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about 'possible data fabrications' and a prior finding that a researcher was 'guilty of data fabrication' in an earlier review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabricated data are a core form of research misconduct; allegations should prompt formal investigation by the institution and can justify retraction of published work if substantiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction when misconduct substantiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Soo-Kyung Kang 'has now retracted four papers amidst questions about image manipulation' and multiple papers are 'in question.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigations validate manipulation or fabrication, journals may issue retractions to correct the literature. Retraction is the appropriate remedy for confirmed serious misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between journals and institutions (COPE guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader comment urging that 'both Journals and Institutions should adhere to COPE Guidelines "Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases".'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and institutions are expected to coordinate on integrity cases per COPE guidance—sharing information, evidence, and timelines—to reach reliable conclusions and manage publications appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding publication pending investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lee told ARS editor Sen to 'hold the Kangs’ April 10 paper from print until the investigation is complete.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may delay printing or further dissemination of articles under inquiry to avoid propagating potentially unreliable results while investigations proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and provision of raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: Author/PI claim that 'my students can also showed the raw data supporting that it was an error.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should retain and be able to produce original/raw data to verify results; availability of raw data can distinguish honest error (correctable by erratum) from misconduct and is central to resolving disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erratum vs retraction as corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Author request: 'I would like to correct it before published it in hard copy of ARS journal... Or if not, this is just a simple error, I would like to publish it's erratum.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an issue is shown to be an honest, isolated error supported by raw data, an erratum may be appropriate; if falsification or pervasive problems are confirmed, retraction is warranted. Editors weigh evidence in choosing corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing evidence and restricting lab access during investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The researchers' labs are 'under lockdown... with all files, notes and computers confiscated by university officials.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should secure potential evidence (files, notebooks, computers) and control access to labs during investigations to preserve integrity of the inquiry and prevent tampering or loss of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of manuscripts under review when concerns arise
rubrics_metrics.description: 'There were two submissions in peer review process which have now been rejected.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may withdraw or reject manuscripts in review if concerns about an author's other work cast doubt on the integrity of submitted material or if investigations reveal problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous whistleblower reports can trigger investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'anonymous whistleblower warned about possible data fabrications' leading to expansion of the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous tips alleging manipulation or fabrication should be evaluated and can legitimately prompt institutional review or journal scrutiny; appropriate processes should be followed to assess credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and limits on disclosure during investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: University official said: 'I am sorry I cannot inform you any because it is strictly classified.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions sometimes place confidentiality or classification on investigation details; while transparency is desirable, privacy/confidentiality rules may limit what can be publicly shared during an active inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls for sanctions for non-cooperation or refusal to act
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader comment: 'And, of course, there should be sanctions in place for those who refuse to do the right thing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders advocate for sanctions against individuals or institutions that refuse to cooperate or that fail to address misconduct; while not a formal policy in this article, the expectation of accountability is a community standard.
